A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasoningBank and MaTTS research. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original WebArena, Mind2Web, and SWE-Bench-Verified experiments, scaling evaluations, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds broader MaTTS evaluations, judge-noise experiments, token-consumption measurements, and Gemma-3-12B-Instruct results.

M1.justification: The memory schema, success/failure extraction, embedding retrieval, append-only consolidation, and parallel/sequential MaTTS procedures remain unchanged. Figure 2 newly depicts the judge explicitly, but that component was already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same WebArena domains, Mind2Web generalization settings, and SWE-Bench-Verified tasks. The added experiments reuse existing task coverage; smaller backbones and simulated judge errors change configurations and controls.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain No Memory, Synapse, and AWM for web tasks, with AWM excluded from software engineering in both versions. Figure 5 retains the same memory comparisons, and the added Gemma evaluation uses the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: Figure 5 changes from three rollouts and Best-of-3 to five rollouts and Best-of-5. V2 also adds controlled ground-truth label flipping across simulated judge accuracies of 50–100%, a Gemma-3-12B-Instruct configuration, token-consumption evaluation, and five-rollout MaTTS pass@1 reporting across WebArena backbones. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: V2 adds a judge-accuracy assessment and controlled verification-noise study in Section 5, a token-cost breakdown in Appendix C.2, and a third case study diagnosing search-query failure in Appendix C.5. Existing failure-trajectory, retrieval-count, and pass@k analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or reports confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. V2's probabilistic label flipping is an experimental control rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged, but Table 1 adds MaTTS overall success rates of 51.8, 56.3, and 48.8 for the three backbones. New results include 72.7% judge accuracy, the noise-sensitivity scores, token totals, and Gemma success rates of 24.1% for ReasoningBank versus 17.1% without memory. Figure 5 replaces three-rollout results with five-rollout results; its changed values do not establish same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The formal agent and streaming-task formulation is unchanged. V2 adds standard formulas for the existing success-rate and average-step metrics, without introducing new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction refocuses the headline effectiveness claim from up to 34.2% improvement for the approaches collectively, citing Figure 4(b), to up to 20% for ReasoningBank, citing Table 1. The central contributions concerning reasoning memory, learning from failures, and memory-aware scaling remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning judge-noise tolerance, token-cost tradeoffs, and applicability to smaller models. Section 4.4 changes its explanation from weaker memories being harmed by scaling to receiving smaller benefits, although it inconsistently retains a statement that their performance decreases. Appendix D expands modular-memory possibilities; the substantive limitations in Appendix E remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a project code location, identifies and links the Gemma checkpoint, and newly states that baselines share retrieval and consolidation mechanisms. It also clarifies step counting. These improve documentation; the PDFs do not establish that baseline implementations changed, and the existing prompts, temperatures, and retrieval defaults are retained.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against instance-level memory approaches and adds works including AutoGuide, Dynamic Cheatsheet, MobileSteward, Skill Set Optimization, and recent memory surveys. It removes the explicit sentence claiming to be first to explore memory-aware scaling. The broader positioning remains similar; publication updates and consolidation of duplicate references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Revisions include localized introduction and related-work rewrites, expanded metric explanations, consistent use of memory extraction terminology, and replacing numbered analysis subsections with descriptive headings. V2 also adds an appendix contents page and an LLM-writing-assistance statement. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the judge-noise plot and failure-diagnosis illustration as Figures 8 and 17, plus cost and smaller-model Tables 5 and 6. It expands Table 1, redraws Figure 2 to show judge-mediated extraction, and updates Figure 5's legend and axis range for Best-of-5. Other displays are retained with relocation, renumbering, or limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of central claims: MaTTS evidence expands beyond one backbone/subset, Figure 8 directly investigates previously untested judge reliability, and Table 5 exposes inference overhead beyond v1's interaction-step accounting. The smaller-model experiment and added code-access information further improve applicability evidence and reproducibility. The revised Figure 5 discussion contains a contradictory claim of baseline deterioration, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains in empirical support and transparency.
